meaning: A copy of a policy's weights that a training run saves along the way. Evaluation decides which checkpoint to keep.
The training objective computed on demonstrations that were held out of training. For a diffusion policy, it is the error in predicting the added noise. It is an open-loop score.

An open-loop score that runs the policy as it runs on the arm on each held-out frame and compares its action with the recorded action, usually as an MSE. It is meaningful only when the number of diffusion steps is held fixed.
Scoring a policy on recorded frames by comparing the action it predicts with the recorded action. The policy's own actions never change what it sees next.
Scoring a policy by letting it drive, on the real arm, in a simulator or in a world model, and counting the successes. Each of its actions changes what it sees next.
The average, over the frames of a recording, of the squared distance between the policy's predicted action and the recorded action.
One complete run of a policy from the starting pose until the task succeeds, fails or runs out of time. It is also called a trial or an episode.
The number of rollouts that ended with the task done, divided by the total number of rollouts.
A number between -1 and 1 that says how closely two lists of numbers rise and fall together. At 1, one list predicts the other exactly. At 0, there is no relation.
The Pearson calculation applied to rank positions. It measures whether two ways of scoring put a set of policies in the same order.
The range of true success rates that could plausibly have produced an observed count. At the 95% level, the range contains the true rate about nineteen times in twenty.
A method for computing a confidence interval on a success rate. It pulls the centre toward one half and keeps the width above zero at 0% and 100%. LeRobot's evaluation tool reports it.
The textbook interval, p plus or minus z times sqrt(p(1-p)/n). It can run past 100%, and it shrinks to zero width at a perfect score.
A test of whether two success counts could come from the same true rate. It counts how often luck alone would split the pooled failures at least as unevenly as the observed split.
How often two equally good policies would show a gap at least as large as the one observed.
The chance that a comparison detects a gap that is really there. At 80% power, the comparison detects the gap four times in five.
The false-alarm rate that a comparison accepts when there is no gap. The 5% level means one false alarm in twenty.

A comparison that is checked after each pair of trials and stops as soon as the evidence is sufficient. It is built so that the repeated checks do not raise the false-alarm rate. STEP (2025) proposes one for robot policies.
A fixed set of simulated tasks that everyone scores on, so that results can be compared.
The state of a benchmark on which nearly every policy scores near the top, so the score no longer separates good policies from poor ones.
A set of simulated manipulation tasks used as a benchmark. It is now saturated. LIBERO-Plus and LIBERO-PRO are successors that perturb the scene.
LeRobot's evaluation tool. It runs a checkpoint in closed loop in a batch of simulated environments and reports the success rate with a 95% Wilson interval.
NVIDIA's evaluation tool for its Isaac Lab simulator. It can run perturbation sweeps over lighting, backgrounds, camera parameters and object mass.
Scoring the same checkpoint across controlled changes to one scene, such as lighting, backgrounds, camera parameters and object mass. You keep only the checkpoints whose success rate holds.
Closed-loop scoring in which a video world model generates what the cameras would show after each action, and a vision-language model judges the generated video.
A model that takes both images and text as input. In world-model evaluation, it judges whether the generated rollout completed the task.
A ranking of policies on real robots, built from blind pairwise comparisons run at seven academic institutions on the DROID platform. Simulators and world models are checked against it.
The robot platform that RoboArena's evaluators share, so that every lab runs the policies on the same model of robot.

expansion: International Conference on Robotics and Automation
meaning: A robotics research conference. The REAL-I robot challenge was held there in 2026.
A robot challenge held at ICRA 2026. Its report names the closed-loop effects that open-loop error misses, and one of its teams used the validation action error to shortlist checkpoints.
The difference between how a policy performs in the simulator and how it performs on the real arm. More simulated trials do not reduce it (section 14).
A simulated environment that steps the physics and gives the policy the joint and object states directly, with no simulated camera. It is the cheapest kind of environment to run.
